chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid, may Allah have mercy on him, reported from his father, who reported from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, who reported from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, who reported from his father, who reported from Ahmad ibn al-Nadhr al-Khazzaz, from Amru ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them) who said:

Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, may Allah be pleased with him, stood near the Ka'bah and called out: 'I am Jundub ibn al-Sakan!' So the people gathered around him. Then he said: 'O people, if one of you intended to travel, he would prepare what is good for him. Do you not then prepare for the journey of the Day of Resurrection what is good for you?'

A man stood up and said to him: 'Guide us, may Allah have mercy on you.' Abu Dharr, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 'Fast on a day of intense heat for the Resurrection. Perform pilgrimage to the Sacred House for Allah the Most High for the great matters. And pray two rak'ahs in the darkness of the night against the loneliness of the graves.'

Let your speech be of two kinds: a word of good that you speak, and a word of evil that you keep silent about. And give charity to a poor person; perhaps it will save you, O poor soul, from a day of anguish.

Let your worldly earnings be two dirhams: one dirham you spend on your dependents, and one dirham you send forward for your hereafter. The third is harmful and of no benefit to you, so do not seek it. And let your worldly pursuits be two: one pursuit in seeking the lawful, and one pursuit for the hereafter. The third is harmful and of no benefit to you, so do not seek it.
Then he said: 'The worry about a day I have not yet reached has killed me.'

key_terms.الكعبة: The Ka’bah — the sacred cubic structure in Mecca, the holiest site in Islam and the direction of prayer
key_terms.حج البيت الحرام: Pilgrimage to the Sacred House — the annual Hajj to Mecca, one of the Five Pillars of Islam
key_terms.درهمين: Two dirhams — silver coins used metaphorically for dividing worldly earnings between family and the hereafter
key_terms.ركعتين: Two rak’ahs — units of Islamic prayer, each consisting of standing, bowing, and prostrating
key_terms.صدقة: Charity (sadaqah) — voluntary charitable giving in Islam, a means of purification and spiritual reward
key_terms.يوم القيامة: The Day of Resurrection — the Islamic eschatological day when all humanity will be resurrected and judged

ai.seo_question: What advice did Abu Dharr al-Ghifari give in his sermon at the Ka'bah about preparing for the Day of Judgement?
ai.summary: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari delivered a famous public sermon at the Ka'bah, where he introduced himself by his real name Jundub ibn al-Sakan to draw attention, then exhorted the people to prepare for the Day of Judgement just as they would prepare for any worldly journey. When a listener asked for specific guidance, Abu Dharr recommended fasting on hot days, performing Hajj pilgrimage, and praying night prayers as spiritual provisions. He then counseled moderation in speech (speaking only good and remaining silent about evil), charitable giving to the poor, and limiting worldly pursuits to two: spending on family and investing for the hereafter. His sermon concluded with a poignant personal reflection on the anxiety of facing a day he had not yet reached, showing the depth of his own fear of the Resurrection. This sermon was delivered at the Ka'bah in the early Islamic period, where Abu Dharr was known for his asceticism and blunt public preaching against worldly attachment.
